value.text:
Qatar University (Arabic: جامعة قطر) is a public research university on the northern outskirts of Doha, Qatar. The institution traces its origins to a College of Education established by an emir's decree in 1973, initially enrolling 150 students. It developed into the University of Qatar in 1977, adding colleges in education, humanities and social sciences, Sharia and law, and science. Engineering followed three years later and business and economics in 1985.

The university offers study in Arabic and English and spans disciplines including arts and sciences, education, engineering, law, Islamic studies, business, pharmacy and medicine. Its history includes the creation of a pharmacy college in 2006, the announced medical college in 2014, and a dental medicine college in 2019. Its research activities include environmental and energy technology work, with laboratories and specialist centres addressing gas processing and transportation safety.

The university recorded 7,660 student registrants in the 2005/06 fall semester and an enrolment of 8,221 in 2009. Later undated descriptions report more than 20,000 students, but these figures belong to different periods and should not be read as a single current count. The institution's programmes and research infrastructure have evolved alongside its expanding academic structure.
